meta.title: Finnish Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 1832 expressions · 492 everyday, 933 idioms, 407 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 1832 Finnish set phrases, idioms and proverbs, in three subdecks: 492 everyday phrases, 933 idioms and 407 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Finnish → English (see the Finnish, recall the meaning) and English → Finnish (see an English meaning, recall the Finnish) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Finnish A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the five, so the two can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the expressions Wiktionary files as phrases or interjections and does not mark as idiomatic — mostly the everyday formulas a Finnish speaker uses as one piece (en tiedä, kuinka paljon, en ymmärrä …). The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (tehdä mieli, olla olemassa, antaa periksi …), most of them verbs, given like every verb in this collection in the first infinitive; and the PROVERBS the sayings Wiktionary files as proverbs (aika on rahaa, rakkaus on sokea, kaikki virtaa …), each glossed with the English proverb that says the same where there is one. Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of Tatoeba's Finnish sentences contain them, an idiom that is a verb being counted with its verb in any form and in either order; only 502 of the 1832 are found there at all, and the rest follow in the order of how common their rarest word is in film and television subtitles. Real example sentences come with 494 of the 1832 expressions, three apiece for 166, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Expressions, meanings and the idiom and proverb labels: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Order: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, then a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba, CC BY 2.0 FR.
